Area.evidence_source: In considering the findings of this and other studies, it must be recognized that gay men seeking therapy for mental health problems are likely to have experienced inner emotional conflict and turmoil from an early age (Bailey & Zucker 1995; Flowers & Buston 2001; PACE 1998; Shildo 1994)., particularly pertinent for gay men who have had negative life experiences (Boon & Miller 1999; Isay 2006; Robertson 1998)., Mental health nurses need to recognize and acknowledge the gendered experiences of their patients (McAndrew & Warne 2005). By way of addressing such experiences, health-care professionals must take cognisance of their response when a patient comes out to them both in terms of their suicidality and their homosexuality., A contemporary psychodynamic approach takes account of the psychosocial existence of the individual, supporting the exploration of the interrelationship created by the merger of the intra-, inter-and extrapsychic worlds. A commitment to long-term therapeutic relationships and the ability to trust would be fundamental to engaging in this type of therapy., Consistency, respect, affirmation, empathy, and staying with and holding the emotional distress are core components to nurturing trust (Green 2003; Isay 2006). Additionally, a gay affirmative stance on the part of a therapist has been found to counteract the effects of homophobia (Lebolt 1999)., In adopting the stance that homosexuality is a natural outcome of human sexual development, it follows that a person's sexual orientation, fantasies, and wishes that constitute their identity should not be challenged, changed, or coerced by a professional ideology that assumes heterosexuality to be the only orientation (Lingiardi & Capozzi 2004).
